description: Create the responsive marketing landing page at web/index.html (+ web/marketing.css + optional web/marketing.js) matching the existing Intention visual identity, and wire a sign-in deep-link into the web app so the marketing 'Sign in' CTA opens the auth modal. Depends conceptually on FEAT-001 (the web app it links to and the deep-link entry point), but the marketing files are otherwise self-contained. The marketing page uses only inline SVG / CSS-drawn mockups - assets/ has NO screenshots, so there must be no to missing files.
steps: Create web/index.html: a semantic, accessible single-page marketing site (header/nav, main with landmark sections, footer). Reuse the design tokens from css/style.css (either link ../css/style.css for :root tokens or redeclare the same custom properties): --bg #f8f9fa, --surface #fff, --text #1a1a2e, --text-muted #6c757d, --primary #4361ee, --primary-hover #3a56d4, --accent #f72585, --border #e9ecef, --radius 10px, shadows, font 'Segoe UI' stack. Do NOT invent a new palette or fonts.

Hero section: product name 'Intention', a one-line tagline, a primary CTA button 'Launch the web app' linking to ../index.html, a secondary CTA 'Download for desktop' linking to https://github.com/sonellmalik/Intention/releases/latest, and a 'Sign in' entry point linking to ../index.html?signin=1. CTAs must be keyboard-focusable and use the existing .btn visual language.

Features section covering the REAL features (from README.md): Pomodoro timer (work/break cycle, customizable), Focus Mode (greyscale), Scheduler (My 5 Priorities + drag time blocks + to-dos/breaks), Distraction tracking & reflection, History heatmap, Articles reader, optional accounts/Online area. Use CSS-drawn / inline-SVG preview cards for any visuals - NO to files that do not exist in assets/.
'How it works' steps section (e.g. 3-4 numbered steps) describing the typical flow (plan the day -> start a focus session -> log distractions -> review history).
A clearly labeled note that some features are desktop-only: system-wide greyscale Focus Mode, the floating mini-timer overlay, and the iOS Focus Companion pairing.
Footer with the GitHub repository link (https://github.com/sonellmalik/Intention) and an MIT license note.

Create web/marketing.css with responsive rules (mobile <=600px, tablet, desktop) so the page looks clean at 375px and 1440px; semantic landmarks, sufficient contrast, visible focus states. Optionally create web/marketing.js for a mobile nav toggle and/or smooth-scroll (keep it tiny and framework-free); omit the file if not needed.

Wire the deep-link in the web app: in index.html's existing bottom inline <script> block, add a small browser-only snippet (guard with !window.electronAPI or simply check the URL) that, on load after auth-ui.js has run, checks for ?signin=1 or #signin and calls window.openAuthModal() (already exposed by js/auth/auth-ui.js). Opening index.html WITHOUT the param must NOT auto-open the modal.
acceptance_criteria: Serving the repo and opening http://localhost:8080/web/ renders a complete marketing page with hero, features, how-it-works, desktop-only note, and footer; there are NO broken-image icons anywhere (no to missing files).

The 'Launch the web app' CTA navigates to the working app (../index.html resolves when served); 'Download for desktop' points at https://github.com/sonellmalik/Intention/releases/latest; the 'Sign in' CTA points at ../index.html?signin=1.
Opening http://localhost:8080/index.html?signin=1 auto-opens the auth modal; opening http://localhost:8080/index.html (no param) does NOT auto-open it.
The page is responsive and clean at both 375px and 1440px, uses the existing color/font tokens, and all CTAs are keyboard-focusable with visible focus.
`npm test` still reports 61 passing / 0 failing (no regression from the index.html inline-script change).
verification: Run `python -m http.server 8080` from the repo root and open http://localhost:8080/web/ ; visually confirm all sections render, no broken images, and the visual style matches the app (colors/fonts from css/style.css).
Click 'Launch the web app' and confirm it loads the working app; inspect the 'Download' and 'Sign in' hrefs for the correct URLs.
Open http://localhost:8080/index.html?signin=1 and confirm the auth modal auto-opens; open http://localhost:8080/index.html and confirm it does not.
Use DevTools responsive mode at 375px and 1440px to confirm the marketing layout is clean and CTAs are reachable by keyboard (Tab + Enter).
Run `npm test` and confirm 61 pass / 0 fail.
findings: DELIVERABLES: created web/index.html, web/marketing.css, web/marketing.js (all new, self-contained). web/index.html links ../css/style.css (reuses :root tokens directly - no palette/font duplication) + marketing.css. Sections: sticky header/nav, hero, features, how-it-works, desktop-only callout, footer. VISUALS: all mockups are inline SVG or CSS-drawn (timer dial, feature cards, history heatmap grid, step numbers); verified 0 tags served - no broken images. CTAs: 'Launch the web app' -> ../index.html (3 occurrences: nav, hero, desktop section), 'Download for desktop' -> https://github.com/sonellmalik/Intention/releases/latest (3), 'Sign in' -> ../index.html?signin=1 (3: nav, hero line, footer). CTAs use the app's .btn/.btn-primary/.btn-ghost classes; marketing.css adds .mk .btn display/padding so anchors render as buttons, plus :focus-visible outlines for keyboard focus. RESPONSIVE: desktop >=1025px = 3-col features / 4-col steps / 2-col hero; tablet 601-1024px = 2-col; mobile <=600px = single column, hero stacks, CTAs full-width, and the nav collapses behind a hamburger (#mk-nav-toggle) toggled by web/marketing.js (tiny, framework-free, progressive-enhancement; closes on link click + Escape; aria-expanded maintained). DEEP-LINK: in index.html's existing bottom inline
